vulnerabilities: Concentration of advanced semiconductor manufacturing in Taiwan (TSMC) — a Chinese military action targeting or blockading Taiwan would immediately shock advanced tech manufacturing worldwide, the US included

Defence industrial base capacity bottlenecks — atrophied shipbuilding capacity and slow munitions replenishment compared to peer adversaries constrain sustained high-rate precision-munition expenditure in a long multi-theatre conflict
Highly digitised, privately operated critical infrastructure (electrical grid, water treatment, financial systems) is exposed to state-sponsored cyber interdiction from China, Russia, and Iran
Large and growing sovereign debt load creates exposure to shifts in international debt-buyer reserve allocation, with knock-on inflation/interest-rate/defence-budget crowding-out risk

Extended Indo-Pacific lines of communication — logistical support for forward-deployed forces in East Asia spans thousands of miles of open ocean, exposed to Chinese long-range missile and submarine interdiction forces in the opening stage of any conflict
strengths: Global blue-water naval force projection — 11 carrier strike groups plus 750+ military facilities across every major theatre
Dollar hegemony and financial-sanctions leverage — control of USD clearing systems, SWIFT routing, and dominant foreign-reserve currency status
Effective monopoly on advanced high-end semiconductor design and IP (chip architectures, EDA design software, leading AI platforms), though physical fabrication is offshored to Taiwan and South Korea
Deep alliance-network architecture (NATO, Quad, AUKUS, Five Eyes) institutionalising collective defence, interoperability, and intelligence sharing
North American energy and agricultural self-sufficiency — net exporter of LNG, crude oil, and primary agricultural commodities
